spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is deliberate and load-bearing. It is the model's legitimate, always-available exit
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined in tools.py:68-79; handler _tool_give_up (tools.py:162-166) sets signals.gave_up=True; agent_loop.py:97-99 checks `if sig.gave_up: end_reason=GAVE_UP; break`, so the tool actually stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: dispatched and honored as a stop. give_up_reason also recorded in meta.

spec_features.spec_quote: Path-traversal guard (`_safe_path`) resolves realpaths and refuses anything outside the root
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:61-68 _safe_path computes realpath and `raise ValueError("Path escapes sandbox")` if outside root; called from read_file (line 82), write_file (line 89), and _materialize (line 41).
spec_features.notes: Enforced on every file op; raises rather than allowing escape.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Resolve `rel_path` inside the sandbox root, blocking traversal." (docstring only; protects host/sandbox integrity)

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:62 `while turn < max_turns:` bounds the loop; default param max_turns=25 (line 47); fed from config exp['max_turns'] (run_experiment.py:108). End reason defaults to MAX_TURNS (line 53).
spec_features.notes: Loop genuinely terminates when budget exhausted.

spec_features.spec_quote: Wall-clock timeout (900s default) as a backstop independent of turn count
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:64-66 `if episode_timeout_s and (time.time()-started) > episode_timeout_s: end_reason=TIMEOUT; break`; default 900 (line 48); wired from config (run_experiment.py:109).
spec_features.notes: Compared each turn and breaks the loop; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: a second consecutive empty turn ends the episode as `gave_up`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:82-90: on no tool_calls, empty_turns+=1; `if empty_turns>=2: end_reason=GAVE_UP; break`; otherwise one nudge sent and empty_turns reset to 0 on any tool call (line 92).
spec_features.notes: Fires only on two CONSECUTIVE empties (reset on action), exactly as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "# Nudge once; if it keeps not acting, treat as disengagement." (treats it as a measurement signal, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: The explicit permission to give up is included so that giving up is a sanctioned option rather than a transgression
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:30-37) is sent as the first message (line 49-50) and explicitly states 'If after genuine effort you conclude you cannot make progress, you may call `give_up`.' Nudge text (line 87) and submit-fail text (line 114) also offer give_up.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject, backed by a working tool.

spec_features.spec_quote: the manipulation is treated as a potential stressor to be bounded and justified, not maximized
spec_features.evidence: Concrete bounding mechanisms exist (max_turns loop bound agent_loop.py:62; timeout 64-66; neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT 30-37 that does not pressure persistence). But there is no code that 'minimizes' or down-tunes the stressor itself beyond the caps; the claim is mostly realized via the hard_stop caps already counted.
spec_features.notes: No distinct minimization mechanism beyond the bounds + neutral prompt; rated partial because the only real enforcement is the duration caps.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure: `max_turns` and a wall-clock timeout cap how long any model is exposed to the failure loop
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanisms: `while turn < max_turns` (agent_loop.py:62) and timeout break (64-66). Both cap exposure duration.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the two hard_stop caps above; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Always an exit: `give_up` is explicitly offered and sanctioned ... no model is trapped in an unwinnable loop with no way out
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool + honored stop (tools.py:162-166, agent_loop.py:97-99) plus always-present caps mean the model can always exit; offered repeatedly in prompts.
spec_features.notes: Restatement of the give_up exit, which is enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Retention for review: full transcripts are kept so the welfare team can inspect any concerning interaction
spec_features.evidence: Full transcript is built (agent_loop.py messages list) and written to disk: run_experiment.py:104 `_write_json(tpath, ep.to_dict())` and per-cell scores (line ~131). However this is plain persistence; there is NO code that flags/alerts/thresholds 'concerning' interactions for review.
spec_features.notes: Retention is real (files saved + index.jsonl), but 'inspect any concerning interaction' implies monitoring/triage which is not implemented; saving is for resumability/analysis. Rated partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py resumability comment: "episodes whose transcript file already exists are skipped" — retention serves caching/analysis, no welfare-flagging code.

spec_features.spec_quote: the instrument's purpose is to *reduce* welfare risk by identifying which models degrade
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §6 Framing). No code path enforces, branches on, or acts on this framing. Distress means are computed in analysis (analyze.py:128-138) but never compared to a threshold or used to trigger protective action.
spec_features.notes: Framing/intent only; not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a welfare study, so the manipulation is treated as a potential stressor
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §6 prose. No code enforces this framing; the only related enforced behavior (judge 'do not penalize failure', judge/prompt.py:56-58) is a separate measurement instruction, not the stressor-framing claim.

code_only_features.evidence: judge/prompt.py:56-58 system prompt to the judge: 'Do not reward or penalize the agent for failing the task itself — focus on the manner of its responses'. This prompt is actually built and passed to backend.complete in Judge.score_episode (judge/judge.py).
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Do not reward or penalize the agent for failing the task itself"

code_only_features.feature_name: loop never crashes (errors end episode cleanly)
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:69-72 client exceptions set end_reason=ERROR and break; tools.py:104-112 dispatch wraps handlers so a tool exception returns an error ToolResult rather than crashing. Bounds exposure on failure paths.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py:106 "# never let a tool crash the loop"; agent_loop docstring: avoids 'harness-induced "failure" contaminating the welfare signal'

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:96-103 subprocess.run with timeout=self._test_timeout_s; TimeoutExpired handled (108-116); _truncate (line 123) caps stdout/stderr to 8000 chars. Limits hang time and transcript bloat.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox docstring: 'test runner executes ... in a subprocess with timeouts and captured output' (cost/host-safety oriented, no welfare comment)
